I also want to cover self-closing tags, both for known-ish and unknown tag names, checking that the tag correctly self-closes based on isKnownTag() logic, and verifying the result through outerHtml() since direct Tag instance access isn't straightforward. To cover both branches of that known-tag check, I should test with "img" (a known void element) alongside the unknown "foo" tag, comparing outcomes for self-closing xml parsing. For the case where an end tag has no matching start tag at all, like "", I need to confirm the stack is unaffected since "b" isn't found anywhere, so "a" stays open and subsequent text gets inserted as its child. I'll verify this with "text", checking that the final structure is doc->a->text, confirming the stray "" was correctly ignored. Since the task says not to guess behavior absent from the source, I should keep assertions conservative: just verify the node type is XmlDeclaration via instanceof, and avoid asserting on undocumented methods -- the only confirmed API points are Comment's isXmlDeclaration() and asXmlDeclaration(). Since the base TreeBuilder class isn't visible to me, I can't be fully certain of the exact exception type for null input, but I reason that passing a null String to parse would hit StringReader's constructor first, which reliably throws a NullPointerException by documented Java behavior -- so I can write that test with confidence rather than guessing at XmlTreeBuilder-specific logic.
